questions.q: What does a report type primarily control?
options: How many people can run the report at once
Which objects and fields a report is allowed to use
Whether the report can be exported to Excel
Which chart colors a report uses
questions.explain: A report type is the template that defines the primary object and the related objects and fields a report can draw from. Everything else (filters, format, charts) works within that boundary.

questions.q: A custom report type relationship is set to "Accounts with or without Opportunities." What does that resemble in SQL?
options: An inner join, keeping only accounts that have opportunities
A UNION of accounts and opportunities
A subquery that counts opportunities per account
A left join, keeping every account whether or not it has an opportunity
questions.explain: "With or without" keeps the primary record even when no related record exists, the same way a left join does. "With" alone behaves like an inner join.

questions.q: A report builder notices a field they need isn't showing up in the Fields pane. What is the most likely cause?
options: The field was deleted from the org
The chosen report type doesn't expose that field
The report format is set to Tabular
The report hasn't been run yet
questions.explain: The Fields pane only ever shows what the chosen report type exposes. Report format (Tabular, Summary, etc.) has nothing to do with which fields are available.

questions.q: When does Salesforce require a custom report type instead of a standard one?
options: Whenever a report needs more than 10 columns
Whenever a report must be scheduled to run nightly
Whenever the report format is Joined
Whenever the object combination a report needs isn't covered by a built-in standard type
questions.explain: Standard report types cover common combinations out of the box. A custom report type is only needed when the object(s) and relationships you want to report on fall outside what Salesforce already ships.

questions.q: Why do experienced admins insist on choosing the report type before anything else when building a report?
options: Because the report type is usually hard to change after the report already exists
Because filters can only be added after the report type is locked by an admin
Because dashboards require a report type to be selected first
Because report types expire after 90 days
questions.explain: Switching report types after a report is built generally means rebuilding the report, since the fields, filters, and groupings may no longer exist on the new type. Choosing it first avoids that rework.
